summary:
ORBITAL: Design, Fly, Discover is a browser-based space mission design game. Players choose a science objective inspired by Europa Clipper, Landsat, or OSIRIS-REx, then build a spacecraft by balancing instruments, mass, power, communications, budget, launcher, and orbit. They pilot the mission, collect science targets, and see how their design choices shaped the outcome.

ORBITAL turns abstract engineering trade-offs into a hands-on learning experience. Its live telemetry, crew play, and post-flight debrief help players connect spacecraft decisions to mission results, while NASA references provide scientific context. The game uses a simplified teaching model—not a real mission-design tool—and encourages players to experiment, compare designs, and learn through replay.
details:
ORBITAL is a browser-based space mission design game. Players choose a science mission, select instruments and spacecraft components, then pilot the spacecraft through an interactive flight. Live telemetry shows how design choices affect resources such as mass, power, budget, and data capacity. During flight, players collect science targets, avoid hazards, manage fuel and hull integrity, and try to return to the communications relay.

The game makes spacecraft design trade-offs tangible. A mission can gather its science and still fail to bring it home, so players can review the outcome, revise their design, and fly again. Our goal is to make space science and mission planning engaging while encouraging players to think about how engineering choices affect scientific results.

We built ORBITAL with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, using the browser Canvas API for flight gameplay. It runs in a modern browser without installation or special hardware. NASA missions provide scientific context for the Europa, Earth observation, and asteroid scenarios. We considered how to make the design choices, controls, and consequences clear to players. In-game resource values and scoring are simplified teaching estimates, not real spacecraft specifications.
